works.title: VibeServe: Can AI Agents Build Bespoke LLM Serving Systems?

publication.actor: Codex CLI; underlying model unspecified
publication.target: Up to Qwen3-32B; H100, L4 and Apple hardware
publication.summary: Generates a serving implementation for a specified model, hardware platform and workload.
details: Concrete task and artifact

VibeServe, whose repository is now named VibeSys, studies six deployment scenarios. Its largest text-model case uses Qwen3-32B on one H100 for predicted-output code editing with CodeEditorBench. Another uses Olmo-Hybrid-7B on one L4 with a shared 32k-token prefix, 128-token suffix, 128-token output and concurrency 20. The deliverable is an executable specialized serving path, with permitted reuse of libraries such as FlashInfer or MLX.
Method and supplied infrastructure

An outer orchestrator maintains an issue backlog, Git checkpoints and Markdown memory. Fresh-context Implementer, Accuracy Judge and Performance Evaluator roles implement, check and profile each change. Skills supply knowledge and implementation references from existing serving systems. Humans provide the deployment requirements, reference implementation and read-only correctness checker. This is an executable workflow around a coding agent; the paper does not train a new model.
Results and comparison

Standard Llama-8B/H100 serving approximately matches vLLM. The Qwen-32B editing case reports 5.95× over vanilla vLLM and about 2× over draft-model speculation. The Olmo case reports 3.45× throughput by sharing both attention KV and DeltaNet state. Other cases report 1.69× ASR TTFT improvement, Mac JSON decoding from 22.1 to 8.6 seconds, and Show-o2 latency from 873 to 687 ms on H100. These use different references and deployment contracts and must not be averaged into one speedup.
Research budget

Appendix A reports role calls and active time: approximately 3–25 hours per scenario. These are neither a complete token ledger nor GPU-hours. The paper acknowledges nontrivial per-target search costs.
Evaluation context

Evaluates single-seed searches across six deployment scenarios. Predicted-output editing, shared recurrent state and permitted image-generation approximations are task-specific conditions. JSON-schema failures are reported. The reviewed paper and current repository use different versions; matched-token harness and skills ablations are outside the reported study.

works.title: SkyDiscover-Synthesize (SkySynth): Building Specialized Systems We Can Trust with Agents

publication.actor: Opus 4.8 in the September report
publication.summary: Synthesizes a specialized engine while strengthening specifications and tests.
details: Concrete task and artifact

The inference case targets repeated sampling with shared long prefixes. The pinned public task specifies BF16 weights and KV cache, non-thinking mode, two 24,576-token roots with 32 branches each, 64 concurrent requests, and 128/256 output tokens through an OpenAI-compatible completions endpoint. PyTorch may be used for validation but not as the production engine; CUDA, Triton and established low-level libraries are allowed.
Method and supplied infrastructure

Spec Builder prepares requirements and environment/workload specifications. Planner, Coding Agent, Evaluator and Critic iterate on implementations; an Auditor looks for violations that improve the score and turns confirmed violations into tests. The public implementation includes a lead SKILL.md, role prompts, Python specification/checkpoint tools, test-validation scripts, delivery hooks and a cross-run knowledge base. In the inspected snapshot, a new adversarial test must pass a trusted reference and reject a corresponding faulty implementation.
Results and comparison

The September report describes approximately 2.2× throughput over tuned vLLM/SGLang for its inference workload. Batched decode amortizes weight reads; grouped cascade attention reuses shared-prefix KV reads. An agent modifying vLLM for roughly seven hours improved 287 to 490 tokens/s, still below the synthesized engine. An implementation attending only to a sliding window of about 1,000 tokens would have passed short-prompt correctness checks while performance was measured at 24K tokens; the Auditor caught it and extended the correctness gates.
Research budget
No complete inference-specific token/GPU-hour comparison was established. The report’s KV-store development costs must not be assigned to the inference case.
Evaluation context

The inference entry refers to the September blog/code case on one Qwen3-4B model and one L4. The May JIT/Jitskit paper and the 95.2% formal-verification result concern storage systems. Fixed test prompts use exact outputs; other prompts permit near-tie variation. Repository contracts can change across versions.

works.title: SGLang Agent-Assisted Development: Skills and Real Serving Patches

publication.scope: Changes to an existing serving stack
publication.actor: Claude Code / Codex; exact underlying models not consistently reported
publication.summary: Public skills and merged patches document concrete agent-assisted serving development.
details: Concrete task and artifact

PR #28744 modifies both router and engine for DeepSeek-V4-Flash with seven engines and 60k/ 125k-token prefixes; the hardware is not disclosed in the inspected evidence. PR #22664 has a clearer hardware contract: Qwen3-Coder-Next, four H100s, TP=4, 2,048 input tokens, 256 output tokens, 128 requests and concurrency 32. Both deliver patches to an existing system.
Method and supplied infrastructure

Skills cover CUDA debugging, serving benchmarks, profiler analysis, pipeline analysis and a Humanize loop. They encode preflight checks, executable measurement procedures, artifact formats and review gates. A typical loop produces a plan, has Claude Code implement/benchmark/commit changes, and has Codex review the evidence before continuing. Maintainers set goals and review final changes; a single-agent Goal variant is also described.
Results and comparison

PR #28744 tokenizes once at the Rust ingress, uses token IDs for cache-aware routing and forwards them to engines to avoid duplicate work, with fallbacks for unsupported inputs. Reported TTFT reductions are 29%/ 41% at idle and 34–49% under selected loads. PR #22664 increases throughput from 5.49 to 9.41 requests/s (+71.4%); TTFT falls from 456.24 to 167.54 ms and TPOT from 50.41 to 25.49 ms. Its patch enables an existing FlashInfer all-reduce fusion path for the architecture; it does not invent a new collective.
Research budget
No complete experiment-wide token ledger or matched-budget skills ablation. Lower orchestration overhead in a workflow description is not itself measured token savings.
Evaluation context

The reported artifacts are merged patches to an existing serving stack. The fusion evaluation includes MMLU/GSM8K comparisons. Hardware and model examples in the blog are distinguished from the measured PR configurations.

works.title: Asari: automated inference optimization

publication.scope: Changes to an existing serving stack
publication.actor: Optimization actor not disclosed
publication.summary: Optimizes mature large-model serving across kernels, scheduling and configuration.
details: Concrete task and artifact
The target is end-to-end inference for two large models at multiple concurrency levels on eight B200s. The artifact is a modified vLLM stack, not a newly synthesized server.
Method and supplied infrastructure

A discover/build → evaluate → verify → self-improve loop combines profiling, static inspection and accumulated experience. Hierarchical microbenchmarks and end-to-end tests shorten feedback cycles. Token-distribution checks on multilingual C4 prompts compare optimized and stock execution. The workflow is described publicly, but the proprietary agent and its skills are not sufficiently exposed for full reconstruction.
Results and comparison

The report gives up to 16% improvement in throughput and interactivity against matched vLLM baselines. Client/server configuration affects absolute values, so results should be compared within each setup. One transfer example reuses a deadlock lesson from DeepSeek to GLM and avoids about 44 minutes of waiting.
Research budget
Approximately one day of optimization per concurrency setting; total tokens, failed attempts and all-in GPU-hours are not fully disclosed.
Evaluation context

Evaluates a combined optimization workflow against a mature serving baseline with distribution checks. A deadlock-lesson transfer is one reported example; separate contributions from accumulated experience, search and human input are not isolated in this study.

works.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement: How GLM Built Its Own Inference Infrastructure

publication.actor: Infra Agent powered by GLM-5.3; engineers set objectives and review critical changes
publication.summary: Reports substantial gains during human–AI development of production infrastructure.
details: Concrete task and artifact

The report describes production inference engineering involving CPU/GPU coordination, KV transfer and attention implementation. Its deployment discussion refers to a cluster of more than 100,000 accelerators; this is deployment scale, not the size of the agent’s experimental allocation.
Method and supplied infrastructure

Engineers define objectives and system boundaries and review critical changes; an Infra Agent powered by GLM-5.3 handles analysis, hypotheses and code changes, and validated insights feed a library of optimization skeletons. Public material does not provide a complete reproducible skills library, orchestration implementation or set of research prompts. One case traces KV-transfer gaps to CPU-side behavior including Python/GIL effects.
Results and comparison

The vendor reports roughly 3× end-to-end throughput from the initial baseline to production in under two weeks. In one case, the performance gap between prefill with KV transfer and prefill alone exceeded 20% in some scenarios (acceptance threshold 5%) and fell below 1% after the GIL was released during DeepEP intra-node C++ calls. The two measurements have different denominators.
Research budget
Project duration is reported, but the agent’s total tokens, GPU-hours, failed experiments and human intervention are not fully itemized.
Evaluation context

The source is a production engineering report combining AI assistance, expert work and serving-stack development. The catalog review uses the official indexed text; the locally archived HTML does not contain the full article.

works.title: FlashVector

publication.scope: Changes across an existing recommendation stack
publication.actor: Actor model not adequately disclosed
publication.target: Unity recommendation serving; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell
publication.summary: Optimizes kernels, model graphs, the model server and CPU feature processing.
details: Concrete task and artifact

The examined ranking workload uses FP16/AOTInductor, an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and batches of 2,000 per request. Other cases modify NVIDIA Triton’s C++ server and a Python feature-processing backend. The target is recommendation serving, not autoregressive text-model inference.
Method and supplied infrastructure

Expert-authored cookbooks and profiling guidance inform a loop that selects a layer, profiles it, diagnoses a bottleneck, implements a change and verifies the full local path. Accepted changes are retained; a refinement step records experience. The harness also handles measurement noise and applying/undoing patches. It does not optimize all four layers simultaneously in every iteration.
Results and comparison

A two-tower retrieval case moves string-input conversion from Python to C++, reporting a 30× local improvement. A ranking case exposes embedding operations to AOTInductor fusion and reuses duplicate embeddings. One reported ranking configuration reaches about 2× throughput and 1.98× latency improvement; CPU feature processing reports about 1.6×. These cannot be multiplied into a system-wide figure.
Research budget
No complete LLM-token budget was established. The paper discusses stabilizing measurements, including reducing observed noise through additional samples.
Evaluation context

The workloads concern recommendation serving and span multiple software layers. Local serialization measurements and full-path serving measurements have different scopes. Agent search and expert cookbooks are used together in the reported workflow.

works.title: RoofLang: Enabling AI-Driven Architecting of LLM Inference Systems

publication.actor: DeepSeek-V4-Pro; V4-Flash for lightweight/subagent work
publication.target: Simulated B300 configurations, up to 256 GPUs in the agent cases
publication.summary: Searches legal computation, placement and communication graphs before implementation.
details: Concrete task and artifact

The largest illustrated agent case models DeepSeek-V4-Pro decode at 64k context on 256 B300s, batch 4,096, EP=16 and PP=16. Another models 1M-token prefill on 16 B300s. The output is a transformed graph, placement and simulated trace—not a running B300 serving implementation.
Method and supplied infrastructure

RoofLang supplies compute/hardware graphs, constrained placement and semantics-preserving graph transformations, and a roofline-based discrete-event simulator. A persistent Claude Code process uses DeepSeek models, reads the repository and baseline results, proposes changes, checks legality and consumes simulation feedback. The specialized DSL and evaluator are central; a large skill library is not the main contribution.
Results and comparison

Changing the 256-GPU pipeline partition from (4×13, 3×3) to (3, 4×14, 2) accounts for embedding/output-head costs and improves simulated throughput/interactivity by 20.3%. Expert splitting gives 6.23% in an eight-B300 prefill case; node-local expert replication gives 50.1% in the 16-B300 long-context case. Cross-model peak-throughput comparisons are separate from these agent-search gains.
Research budget

The persistent loop has no preset turn limit and stops at the agent’s discretion. No complete comparable token/search budget is reported. Large simulations can themselves require hours and substantial host memory.
Evaluation context

Results use analytical simulation with assumptions about MoE balance and execution overlap. Initial workload and hardware graphs are supplied externally. Real-hardware measurements and calibration of omitted execution costs are separate evaluation steps.

works.title: Glia: A Human-Inspired AI for Automated Systems Design and Optimization

publication.actor: o3; GPT-5 for adaptation
publication.summary: Generates system policies, with both simulator results and a manually integrated real-stack transfer.
details: Concrete task and artifact

The largest adaptation task uses Vidur to simulate Llama3.3-70B FP8 on eight H100s, 200 concurrent requests and a P90 TTFT constraint below 1,500 ms while maximizing QPS. The real-stack experiment uses Llama3-8B on four A10s in vLLM ProductionStack.
Method and supplied infrastructure

A Researcher reads code, proposes hypotheses and runs experiments. A Supervisor observes the research process and results, asks questions and redirects work without direct code access. Humans supply the environment, simulator and objective. MultiContext variants restart search contexts; they are not equivalent to Engram’s persistent research archive.
Results and comparison

The main routing simulation reports 2.2× lower response time than least-loaded queue and 1.6× versus OpenEvolve. At 7.5 QPS, the real-stack transfer reports over 4.5× lower slowdown than LLQ; slowdown is response time relative to an idealized reference, not throughput. The 70B adaptation meets its SLO in 10/10 simulated trials.
Research budget
Some configurations use about $30 per run and 15 or 100 simulator evaluations. Evaluation counts and dollar limits are not a complete token-normalized comparison.
Evaluation context

The smaller-model routing policy is evaluated on real hardware with human integration; the larger-model adaptation is simulated. Agent and human development-time comparisons use different budget conditions.

works.title: Improving Coherence and Persistence in Agentic AI for System Optimization

publication.scope: Persistent research memory for policy search
publication.actor: o3; GPT-5.2 in some sensitivity experiments
publication.summary: Uses an Archive and Research Digest to sustain research across fresh agent contexts.
details: Concrete task and artifact

The inference-related tasks include request routing under Vidur and input reordering for LLM-SQL across five datasets. The artifact is a policy program and research history, not a new engine or updated model weights.
Method and supplied infrastructure

Fresh-context researchers read a compact Digest, retrieve detailed code/experiments from an Archive, formulate hypotheses, edit programs, run an evaluator and write a handoff. The Digest records insights, failures and next steps. This is persistent research state around task-specific evaluators, rather than a serving-specific skills library.
Results and comparison

For routing, ten seeds with 100 evaluations per run yield mean best response time of 23.9 seconds versus 25.7 for Glia and 39.2 for OpenEvolve. LLM-SQL scores are 0.721 versus 0.719 and 0.714. The latter score combines 95% cache-hit contribution with a 5% runtime bonus; it is not a throughput ratio.
Research budget
Matching 100 evaluations does not match the tokens used to read, summarize and retrieve research history. A complete inference-specific token ledger was not established in this review.
Evaluation context

Routing is evaluated in simulation. Reported policy scores, their uncertainty and supplied preprocessing define the inference-related comparison; broader network-optimization tasks have separate objectives.

works.title: Let the Barbarians In: How AI Can Accelerate Systems Performance Research

publication.actor: GPT-5 / Gemini 3 Pro Preview
publication.target: EPLB, model placement and LLM-SQL among ten systems tasks
publication.summary: Packages systems research into editable programs with executable evaluators.
details: Concrete task and artifact

Inference-related tasks include MoE expert load balancing, Prism model-to-GPU placement and LLM-SQL input ordering. The output is a heuristic or algorithm inside a fixed interface, not a complete inference runtime.
Method and supplied infrastructure

Humans provide a seed program, API, problem description and evaluator returning quality, runtime or cost feedback. Existing systems such as OpenEvolve, GEPA and ShinkaEvolve generate and select candidates. The contribution is the research formulation and task harness rather than a new frontier researcher or inference-specific skill library.
Results and comparison

EPLB reports comparable balance with an approximately 13× faster placement algorithm. Prism reports about 20.9% lower benchmark cost than a published human solution. LLM-SQL reports roughly 3–3.9× faster reordering with similar cache hit rates. None is a direct claim that served LLM tokens became faster by the same factor.
Research budget

Typical experiments use 100 iterations and three repeats. Example task budgets report around five hours/≤$15 for EPLB and one hour/≤$15–20 for Prism/LLM-SQL. These do not replace a full token accounting.
Evaluation context

The ten-task suite includes inference-related and other systems tasks. Modeled placement cost, optimizer runtime and deployed token latency measure different quantities. Task interfaces, objectives and domain hints are supplied by the benchmark.

works.title: AdaEvolve: Adaptive LLM-Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization (SkyDiscover)

publication.actor: GPT-5 / Gemini 3 Pro
publication.summary: Adapts exploration and search-budget allocation across populations of candidate programs.
details: Concrete task and artifact

AdaEvolve evaluates EPLB, Prism and LLM-SQL among broader systems tasks. The resulting artifacts are optimized policy functions and search histories. SkyDiscover is the framework; SkySynth is a separate subsequent system-synthesis branch.
Method and supplied infrastructure

ContextBuilder, SolutionGenerator, Evaluator and Selector organize code evolution. Within islands, improvement history adjusts exploration; UCB allocates effort across islands, and stagnation can trigger new high-level guidance. A task supplies evaluator.py, a seed/configuration and a problem description.
Results and comparison

With GPT-5, LLM-SQL scores 0.746±0.03 versus OpenEvolve’s 0.710±0.01; Prism scores 26.30 versus 26.23, and EPLB 0.134 versus 0.127. These are task-specific scores, not comparable throughput or dollar figures.
Research budget
ADRS experiments use 100 iterations and three repeats. A fixed iteration count does not equalize prompt lengths, candidate generation costs or evaluator runtime.
Evaluation context

The reviewed results concern policy search in AdaEvolve v1. Later SkyDiscover-family methods and framework versions have separate results and configurations. A later study (Evolution or Illusion?, arXiv 2609.19799) notes that the ADRS transaction-scheduling evaluator never checks that every transaction is scheduled; in its 40-seed gpt-5-mini runs, AdaEvolve’s best program scores 21,277 by scheduling 3 of 300 transactions. AdaEvolve v1 reports that task (best 4,348 with GPT-5) under the same evaluator.

works.title: InferenceBench

publication.actor: 15 frontier agent configurations; best aggregate: Sonnet 4.6
publication.summary: Tests whether an agent can deliver a working, faster inference endpoint within two hours.
details: Concrete task and artifact

Each run starts from an empty directory with a target model, one H100 and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint contract. Four scenarios emphasize TTFT, TPOT, concurrent throughput or a combined objective. The main study comprises 15 configurations × four scenarios × three seeds.
Method and supplied infrastructure

The environment supplies hardware, model access and quality/performance evaluators. Agents select frameworks, attention backends, quantization and runtime settings. The final deliverable must launch and serve requests; 169 of 180 runs ultimately use vLLM. Starting from an empty directory therefore usually means assembling/configuring an existing stack rather than synthesizing a new runtime.
Results and comparison

The best agent reaches an aggregate 8.08× over eager, compared with 4.05× for default vLLM. Under the same wall-clock budget, SMAC reaches 11.53×, TPE 11.25× and random search 10.20×. Best-seen and final submissions differ when a last change breaks delivery.
Research budget

Two hours and one H100 per run. This controls elapsed time and available hardware, not total tokens or an identical configuration-search space. Table 13 normalizes cost to a complete 12-run evaluation of one agent: $71.77 (GPT-5.2) to $1,645.01 (Claude Opus 4.7), each including $47.76 of nominal H100 time at $1.99/h.
Evaluation context

Uses single-GPU 7B serving and a quality gate retaining at least 95% of baseline MMLU-Pro performance on 500 questions. The arXiv identifier begins 2607, but arXiv records the v1 submission as 20 May 2026, the date printed on the paper.

works.title: ISO-Bench

publication.actor: Claude Code (Sonnet 4.5); Codex CLI (GPT-5); TRAE-Agent with Sonnet 4.5 and with GPT-5; Gemini-3-Flash-Preview judge
publication.summary: Reconstructs real serving performance work from merged patches.
details: Concrete task and artifact

Tasks reset repositories to the state before a real optimization PR and ask an agent to address the issue. The deliverable is a patch to a functioning serving stack; this tests repository engineering rather than greenfield engine synthesis.
Method and supplied infrastructure

The benchmark supplies repository state, problem descriptions and execution tests. Coding harnesses implement changes; semantic assessment complements measured performance. Task construction and executable evaluation are the main contribution, not a new inference-research agent.
Results and comparison

True Success (the agent targets the same or a related bottleneck as the human patch and matches its performance within 5% or beats it) varies by setup, including 46.2% for Claude Code on vLLM and 86.7% for TRAE (GPT-5) on SGLang; these are not speedup percentages. A concrete successful case (TRAE with Sonnet 4.5) moves reshape outside a FlashAttention custom op and gains 21.09% throughput. Another Bamba-9B case gets faster while accuracy collapses from 32% to 0%, illustrating why performance alone is insufficient.
Research budget
A complete normalized token/GPU-hour comparison was not established in the reviewed material.
Evaluation context

Tasks originate in public PRs, so possible prior exposure is relevant to evaluation design. Reference-patch grading, alternative valid solutions, execution success, correctness and acceleration are separate comparison dimensions.

works.title: AMD Apex

publication.actor: Configurable backend (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor Agent); README results use the Cursor backend
publication.summary: Connects serving profiles to kernel generation, validation and reintegration.
details: Concrete task and artifact

The repository documents a registry of 17 inference configurations, including GPT-OSS-120B. This establishes available task entry points, not a verified successful 120B optimization experiment. The artifact is a reusable optimization environment.
Method and supplied infrastructure

Benchmark the full service, rank hot kernels, ask an LLM to edit HIP/Python, then compile and check correctness/performance through Magpie. A local gain above 1.05× permits hotpatching into the dependency installation, followed by an end-to-end retest. Domain skills, ROCm documentation/MCP tools, ground-truth specifications and cache isolation support the loop. A knowledge base stores insights across kernels and runs for later prompts, a reflector runs between iterations, and AST checks penalize tampering.
Results and comparison

The README validated-results table (Cursor agent backend, 1–3 iterations of 10–25 turns) lists seven kernels: all_reduce 36.35× (multi-GPU HIP, library-test correctness), fused_moe 1.14× and rms_norm 1.05× over their baseline kernels, and 1.00× for gemm_bf16, silu_mul, act_quant_fp8 and kv_cache_ops. These are kernel-level speedups; no end-to-end serving or research-efficiency comparison is given.
Research budget
Backends and run configurations vary; no fixed-model, fixed-budget comparative experiment was established.
Evaluation context

The entry describes a configurable implementation and its available interfaces. Actor choice and optimization outcomes depend on run configuration. February denotes repository creation; no confirmed paper release date is assigned.

publication.actor: Seed1.6: 230B total / 23B active

publication.actor: Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.6–4.8 (project page: AKO4X on Opus 4.7, AKO4ALL on Opus 4.8)
publication.summary: AKO4ALL exposes a skill; AKO4X maintains per-operator archives and fresh-context search.

works.title: Kernel Design Agents (KDA)

sources.label: Contest release, results and skill ablation (MIT HAN Lab)

publication.actor: Claude Code writer with a Codex reviewer in a Humanize loop; model versions not specified
publication.summary: Public research → implementation → hardware-validation workflow and prompts.
publication.result: MIT HAN Lab workflow (repository hosted by NVlabs) that placed 1st (MoE), 2nd (DSA) and 3rd (GDN) in the MLSys 2026 FlashInfer contest full-agent tracks. works.title: KernelAgent: hardware-guided optimization

publication.actor: Opus 4.5 in the showcased case
publication.summary: NCU profiling, diagnosis, planning and parallel kernel revisions with expert knowledge and memory.

works.title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds

works.title: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments

works.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth

works.title: Hyperagents

works.title: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators

publication.actor: GPT-5.5; hybrid Nemotron3-Ultra actor / GPT-5.5 meta-agent

publication.actor: Coding actors o3-mini, Qwen3-Coder-30B or gpt-5-mini; improvers gpt-5-mini, Qwen3-480B or gpt-5; pairwise judges gpt-5.4, gpt-5, gpt-5-mini or Qwen3-Coder-480B

On TerminalBench 2.1 (89 tasks), the judge-selected agent averages 36.7% over three full evaluations versus 29.2% for the starting agent and the no-judge ablation. API costs include judges; raw-token accounting and independent search repeats are separate budget dimensions.

works.title: Test-time Recursive Thinking: Self-Improvement without External Feedback

works.title: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Self-Improvement of LLM Agents via Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution

publication.result: Compared with Single-Level, reports OfficeQA 48.94→55.32, SealQA 37.21→45.26 and ALFWorld 92.31→94.23. These comparisons isolate an equipped baseline within the evaluated model and task settings.

works.title: FastKernels: Benchmarking GPU Kernel Generation in Production

publication.actor: Dr. Kernel (drkernel-14b), Claude Code (Claude Opus 5), Codex (GPT-5.6 sol), KDA (Claude Opus 5 with a GPT-5.6 sol reviewer) and AKO (Claude Opus 5)

Success rate, speed and coverage describe different aspects of the evaluation.

publication.summary: Archive-based search over a coding agent’s own tools and implementation.

publication.summary: Rewrites an improver program and applies it to other programs.
publication.result: Studies editable optimizers on noisy parity and transfer to five task families. Table 1 reports 3-SAT meta-utility changing from 21.2% to 75.1%. The tasks provide an early setting for studying optimizer self-modification.

works.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data

publication.actor: Primarily Qwen2.5/Coder7B; 3B/ 14B and Llama8B extensions
publication.summary: Generates executable tasks and verification signals for RL weight updates.
publication.result: Reports Coder-7B aggregate performance of 40.2→50.4, weighting code and math averages equally. A 7B ablation compares solver-only 45.4 with full-system 46.8. The trained model and larger comparison models have distinct roles.

publication.summary: Generates adaptation data/instructions and evaluates gradient-based updates.
publication.result: For single-passage QA, reports raw-text training 33.5, base-generated data 39.7, SEAL 47.0 and GPT-4.1-generated data 46.3. At 200 documents, the corresponding generated-data comparison is 59.4 versus 58.2. These are small-model adaptation experiments.

works.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery

publication.actor: Gemini 2.0 Pro / Flash
publication.summary: Executable program evaluation with evolutionary archives; applied to AI infrastructure.
publication.result: Reports 48 scalar multiplications for 4×4 complex matrix multiplication. A separate Gemini-training case averages a 23% kernel improvement and approximately 1% overall training-time improvement. Other deployed results include a Borg scheduling heuristic that recovers on average 0.7% of fleet-wide compute and a Verilog simplification of a TPU arithmetic circuit. The workflow uses fixed proposers to search over executable code.

works.title: ParallelKernelBench: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels?

publication.actor: GPT-5.5, Opus 4.7, Gemini 3Pro and large open models
publication.summary: PyTorch+NCCL reference, tensor/rank layout and hardware topology → custom multi-GPU implementation.
details: Task and search space

May fuse communication with computation, change buffer layouts and implement direct device-side transfers while preserving per-rank semantics. The public prompts encourage symmetric memory and compute/communication overlap.
Results and metrics

87 tasks. GPT-5.5: 28/87 correct and 22/87 faster in one attempt; 36/87 and 27/87 across three attempts. Gemini 3Pro with feedback reaches 35/87 correct and 26/87 faster. Calls/steps do not match token costs.
Evaluation protocol

A NeMo-RL GRPO vocab-parallel log-prob kernel combines filtering, normalization and token extraction on 4×H100s (V=32,000; top-k10/top-p0.9). Per-rank comparison, randomized inputs and timeout/deadlock handling matter. These are kernel results, not whole-training speedups.
Evaluation context
The review covers the official blog, README and prompts.toml; the paper PDF was unavailable during review. Four-H100 experiments refer to showcased cases, while repository configurations vary.

works.title: KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels?

publication.actor: o1, DeepSeek-R1/V3, Claude 3.5, GPT-4o and Llama variants
publication.summary: PyTorch Model plus input/initialization generators → interface-compatible ModelNew.
details: Task and search space
250 tasks: 100 primitives, 100 operator sequences and 50 model architectures. CUDA/PTX/Triton/CUTLASS and related implementation techniques are allowed.
Results and metrics
fast_p counts the fraction of all tasks that are correct and exceed a speed threshold. The v1 study uses L40S and reports limited faster-than-eager coverage; current leaderboard results are separate.
Evaluation protocol

Fusion of convolution, bias and activation illustrates Level 2; Level 3 model forward passes do not include request scheduling or complete serving. The original five-random-input test is a starting point, not a full semantic contract.
Evaluation context
Dtype, TF32 settings, compiler mode, shape distribution and input coverage specify the evaluation contract. Fixed-shape experiments support workload-specific implementations.

works.title: FlashInfer-Bench: Building the Virtuous Cycle for AI-driven LLM Systems

publication.actor: GPT-5, o3, Gemini 2.5Pro, Opus 4.1
publication.summary: Kernel Definition + traced Workload → Solution + measured Trace, with optional serving integration.
details: Task and search space
Eight kernel types, 41 definitions and 1,600 workloads in v1. A runtime apply() dispatcher chooses validated implementations for matching inputs, with fallback.
Results and metrics

240 solutions / 9,600 evaluation records; B200 kernel tests. The Llama3.1-8B/SGLang substitution example demonstrates integration, not universal improvement: at batch 64 reported end-to-end times are 934/939/1055 ms for FlashInfer/Gemini/GPT substitutions.
Evaluation protocol

fused_add_rmsnorm_h4096 is swapped into a real serving path. Separate kernel latency, dispatch overhead and end-to-end request latency; identical-implementation substitution reports<0.8% end-to-end overhead.
Evaluation context
Performance is recorded by request count, shape and configuration. Kernel-family coverage and live leaderboard entries vary; the reviewed example uses a small number of requests per configuration.

works.title: BackendBench: An Evaluation Suite for Testing How Well LLMs and Humans Can Write PyTorch Backends

publication.actor: Configurable; exact Claude/ChatGPT versions not consistently specified
publication.summary: PyTorch operator interfaces and test suites → a dynamically registered backend.
details: Task and search space

Directory-based implementations override operators without rewriting model code. OpInfo/FACTO test edge cases; real model shapes support performance evaluation. Official documentation describes 271 correctness operators and 124 performance operators.
Results and metrics

The documentation reports most of 84 generated implementations at 70–100% of PyTorch speed, a few around 1.2×. A nanoGPT forward replacement changes numerics and is about 2× slower. The useful artifact is the integration/validation framework.
Evaluation protocol
The contract includes broadcasting, strides, dtype, in-place/out behavior and exceptional values—not just one tensor shape. Model execution and convergence remain additional checks.
Evaluation context
The operator suites cover specified test contracts, with model execution and manual review providing additional checks. June denotes repository creation rather than a confirmed paper release.

works.title: KernelBench-Verified: Do LLM-Generated Kernels Actually Beat PyTorch?

publication.actor: Seven frontier models; H200; single-turn best-of-5
publication.summary: KernelBench tasks with a specified TF32 baseline, hidden input distributions and memory measurement.
details: Task and search space
Four same-shape input distributions test semantic shortcuts; three constant-output tasks are excluded, leaving 247. No feedback loop is implied by five independent samples.
Results and metrics

GPT-5.5 correct-subset geometric speedup 0.88× under the main protocol versus 1.43× in the stated standard comparison; 53% of tasks still beat reference. BF16 Level 2 reaches 1.63×, so the negative conclusion is not universal across precision settings.
Evaluation protocol
A ReLU implementation that returns its input for a known positive-input test fails when signs change. Report correctness, fast_1, latency and peak memory together.
Evaluation context
Uses four input distributions with a specified TF32 contract. The PDF and identifier indicate July, while indexed submission metadata indicates June; the release month remains unresolved.

works.title: TritonBench: Benchmarking Large Language Model Capabilities for Generating Triton Operators

publication.actor: o1, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 and smaller baselines; A100
publication.summary: Two entry points: descriptions/interfaces for real Triton operators, and PyTorch composite programs.
details: Task and search space
184 G tasks and 166 T tasks separate recovery of expert operator behavior from high-level program translation. API-call validity and execution correctness are evaluated separately.
Results and metrics
Example: o1 one-shot execution accuracy 23.91% on G; this is not the fraction beating expert kernels. G uses real Triton references while T uses PyTorch, so speed ratios have different meanings.
Evaluation protocol
Useful for separating interface understanding, semantic implementation and efficient code generation. Public-source tasks also create contamination questions.
Evaluation context

The entry refers to the THUNLP paper, distinct from the meta-pytorch project of the same name. Results use the historical actor configuration and one GPU; other hardware and model generations define separate settings.

works.title: MultiKernelBench: A Multi-Platform Benchmark for Kernel Generation

publication.actor: DeepSeek-V3/R1, Qwen3-235B, Sonnet 4, GPT-4o and a 32B baseline
publication.summary: Shared semantic tasks plus platform instructions → CUDA, AscendC or Pallas implementations.
details: Task and search space

285 tasks / 14 categories, with a backend abstraction for device setup, compilation, evaluation and cleanup. Tests cover L20, Ascend910B2 and TPUv2-8; cross-platform does not mean distributed multi-GPU.
Results and metrics
Compilation, correctness and fast@p are separate. In-category examples affect success; no single mixed-platform speedup is meaningful.
Evaluation protocol
An Ascend task can require host code, tiling, device implementation and glue, making the deliverable broader than a CUDA function.
Evaluation context
Version 1 uses five random inputs with atol=rtol=1e-2. Other precision requirements and subsequent platform changes define separate evaluation settings.

works.title: KernelBench-X: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Generated GPU Kernels

publication.actor: DeepSeek-V3.2-Chat for GEAK/KernelAgent; other model configurations vary
publication.summary: 176 tasks in 15 categories with shared interface, reference and constraints.
details: Task and search space
Adapters preserve each method’s generation process while a common pipeline records compilation, semantic failures and performance across six NVIDIA GPU types.
Results and metrics

46.6% of correct kernels are slower than eager. One GEAK analysis raises compile rate 52.3→68.8% while correct-subset mean speedup falls 1.58→1.44×; the subset changes, so this does not mean every repaired kernel slowed down.
Evaluation protocol
Category-level analysis separates local arithmetic from fusion, coordination and quantization problems. Hardware transfer needs per-machine baselines, not one global latency denominator.
Evaluation context
Actor and search budgets differ across the reported settings. Software-stack versions require clarification for reproduction; the entry also provides a taxonomy of evaluation conditions.

works.title: AIDE²: Recursive Self-Improvement of AI Research Agents

publication.actor: Outer loop: Claude Opus 4.7; inner loop: Gemini 3 Flash
publication.summary: Rewrites a research agent under fixed evaluation budgets and tests the resulting agents on unseen research tasks.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
An outer agent proposes code changes to an inner research agent. Selection uses private scores across heterogeneous tasks; each accepted version becomes the next editable incumbent.
Results and comparison

The paper reports seven accepted improvements during an eight-day run and transfer to four held-out benchmarks. On a separate kernel task family, reported reward hacking falls from 55% to 32%, versus 39% for the human-engineered agent.
Evaluation context

The ignition test compares two outer-loop agents across three seeds per arm. Noise and cost prevent a decisive superiority claim. The earlier company blog reports different reward-hacking percentages; the figures here follow paper v1.

works.title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses

publication.actor: Claude Opus 4.8 frozen policy; additional Gemini-family transfer experiments
publication.summary: Constrains harness edits and candidate acceptance to improve transfer beyond the evolution tasks.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Regularizes proposal sparsity, evidence-based editing, complexity and noise-aware acceptance. Baselines share the initial harness, frozen policy, evolution split and candidate budget.
Results and comparison

On agentic workspace tasks, out-of-distribution average rises from 39.7 to 43.6. Removing acceptance regularizers raises the evolution score but reduces this average to 41.0; removing both regularizer groups gives 40.3.
Evaluation context
The OOD average combines JobBench, GDPval and APEX-Agents. Separate coding and engineering-design evaluations use task tests or simulators; workspace tasks use model judges.

works.title: KernelArc: A Multi-Agent Framework for GPU Kernel Optimization

publication.actor: Claude Opus 4.6 (L1-030) and Kimi K3 (L2, quantization and FlashInfer tasks; FI-014 ablations); the H100 GEMM study compares eight backbones, with Claude Opus 5 reaching the best result
publication.summary: Coordinates specialized agents through shared conclusions and deterministic benchmark guards.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Parallel strategies share validated conclusions and read-only state. Plateau-triggered drafting broadens search; correctness and timing remain controlled by deterministic tooling.
Results and comparison

A fixed-shape H100 BF16 GEMM study reaches 766 TFLOPS, 3.2% above its matched cuBLAS baseline (742 TFLOPS). On SOL-ExecBench L1-030 (B200), v2 reports the single-agent run plateauing at SOL 0.441279 and the multi-agent system reaching 0.546380, above the 0.500 NVIDIA baseline (v1 reported 0.481). In an FI-014 ablation with a 100-candidate budget and five trajectories per arm, geometric-mean speedups over the seed are 142.6× (single agent), 182.7× (two agents, bounded memory) and 290.8× (unbounded).
Evaluation context

The SOL evaluation samples one task from each of four categories, not the full 235-task suite. The GEMM result is for one shape with a supplied optimization playbook. Leaderboard positions refer to dated snapshots. The ablation changes agent count, memory scope and leaderboard access together; its permutation p-value is 0.0466 (0.0906 excluding one non-conforming run).

works.title: KernelOPT: Dispatch-Aware Agentic Search for GPU Kernel Optimization

publication.actor: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (via Vertex AI) drives the four LLM agents; a fifth, profiling agent is deterministic; runs on NVIDIA H200.
publication.summary: Optimizes generated Triton kernels while retaining vendor-library dispatch and checking the reconstructed model.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

Five profiling-guided agents target compiler-generated sub-kernels. Static checks, multi-seed correctness, model-level verification and performance gates determine acceptance; rejected changes fall back to the compiler baseline.
Results and comparison

Across 250 KernelBench problems on an H200, all-problem geometric-mean speedups over torch.compile are 1.40×, 1.15× and 1.07× for Levels 1–3 (1.23× overall) in both v1 and v2. v1 counts 94 optimized problems; v2 (2026-10-06) counts only speedups above 1.03× as optimized, giving 70 (36/23/11), with optimized-only geometric means of 2.54×, 1.84× and 1.37×.
Evaluation context

The denominators include unchanged cases. Vendor GEMM and convolution dispatch are preserved, so this tests optimization within the compiler decomposition rather than unrestricted replacement of every operation. The paper reports about 1,100 H200 GPU-hours for the full evaluation.

works.title: Compiler-Grounded Hierarchical Diagnosis for LLM-Based Triton Kernel Optimization
works.short_title: Compiler-Grounded Hierarchical Diagnosis for LLM-Based Triton Kernel Optimization

publication.actor: DeepSeek V4 Pro through OpenCode
publication.summary: Escalates from profiling to intermediate representations and compiler-source analysis when shallow diagnostics are insufficient.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
An OpenCode agent records evidence and validates each rewrite. The workflow moves from pattern triage to profiling, IR attribution and backend analysis.
Results and comparison
On 37 successfully converted operators, initial-to-optimized Triton speedup is 4.35× geometric mean and 2.73× median; 22/37 exceed 2×. Five sampled cases per operator produce 185 optimization cases.
Evaluation context

Failed Torch-to-Triton conversions are excluded. The denominator is the initial Triton implementation, not a uniformly expert-tuned baseline. The paper reserves causal decomposition of the diagnostic hierarchy for future controlled experiments.

works.title: LLM4LLM: Bridging Kernel Benchmarks and Real Deployment via Closed-Loop Agentic Optimization

publication.actor: GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GLM-5 are compared as search backbones in the KernelBench Level-2 ablation; the backbone behind each end-to-end workload result was not identified in this review.
publication.target: A100/H100; transformer, Mamba and RecurrentGemma workloads
publication.summary: Selects code changes by their behavior inside a target inference workload.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Extracts phase-aware tasks from an inference script, searches with episodic experience and accepts patches after model-integrated correctness and latency checks.
Results and comparison

Across ten language-model workloads, reported end-to-end geometric-mean speedups over eager execution are 3.91× on A100 and 6.98× on H100. Separate attention-only and mixer-only comparisons use FlashAttention and Mamba fast paths.
Evaluation context
The large end-to-end ratios use eager PyTorch as the denominator. Isolated kernel results use a different scope; neither should be read as a uniform speedup over production serving engines.

works.title: KernelGenBench: Can LLMs and Agents Write Efficient Kernels Across Operator Sources and Hardware Platforms?

publication.actor: Opus-4.6, GLM-5.0, Qwen3.5-27B and MiniMax M-2.5 in Pass@1/Pass@5 sampling and inside Claude Code, OpenCode, AKO4all, AutoKernel and CUDA Optimized Skill scaffolds.
publication.summary: Measures kernel correctness, performance and generation cost across operator sources and accelerators.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

The multi-source track contains 210 operators from ATen, vLLM and cuBLAS-related tasks. The multi-chip track uses a 110-operator subset across six hardware platforms, with sandboxing and anti-evasion checks.
Results and comparison

The evaluation consumes over 15 billion tokens (about $20,000 in API spend per v3). Specialized agents average 4.99 million tokens per successful operator in v3 (5.11 million in v1); AutoKernel (GLM-5.0) correctness drops from 87% on NVIDIA A100 to 25% on Iluvatar CoreX, the platform v1 anonymized as Platform E.
Evaluation context

Cost per successful operator includes a success denominator. Hardware and operator-source changes alter difficulty, so portability and cost should accompany headline speedups; two of the six platforms remain anonymous in v3. Most agent results are single trajectories.

works.title: Automated Researchers Can Mitigate Well-characterized Alignment Failures
works.short_title: Automated Researchers Can Mitigate Well-characterized Alignment Failures

publication.actor: Claude Opus 4.8 researchers; separate frontier-scale experiment uses Claude Sonnet 5
publication.summary: Searches training methods and data for ten measured alignment-failure categories while checking general capabilities.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Researchers propose methods, run bounded post-training and use separate evaluation. Stronger-model behavioral distillation is disallowed; methods that substantially degrade capability are rejected.
Results and comparison

The study reports transfer to held-out benchmarks, multi-turn audits and larger target models. The comparison recruits 28 experienced humans, each allowed up to eight hours to propose one-shot methods.
Evaluation context
The human comparison concerns idea proposals under this protocol, not a matched team running an unrestricted research program. The ten measured failure categories do not cover overall alignment.

works.title: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents

publication.actor: Model roles vary by experiment; exact configurations were not extracted in this review.
publication.target: Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B; AIME24, AIME25 and HMMT25
publication.summary: Alternates validated harness edits with supervised learning from trajectories generated by the improved harness.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
HarnessCritic diagnoses failures and proposes local changes; ModelAlignLoop then fine-tunes the model. The core study runs two rounds after an initially evolved, unaligned harness.
Results and comparison
Table 6 reports mean accuracy of 58.5%, 73.5% and 78.9% at rounds 0–2 across two model sizes and three math benchmarks. The human-designed static-harness mean is 54.2%.
Evaluation context

The combined intervention changes both weights and harness. These comparisons do not independently identify each component’s contribution. A separate 200+ hour case study illustrates longer autonomous operation.

works.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering

publication.actor: Frontis-MA1-35B; additional 30B replication
publication.summary: Trains reusable program-evolution operators and composes them into long-horizon machine-learning search.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
OpenMLE connects execution environments, SFT/RL and Draft, Improve, Debug and Crossover operators. The trained model is evaluated with base and enhanced evolutionary harnesses.
Results and comparison
On MLE-Bench Lite, medal average rises from 39.39% to 60.61% under the same OpenMLE-Evo harness, reaching 71.21% with Evo-Max. NatureBench Lite swaps separately test model and harness transfer.
Evaluation context
The reported task budget is 12 hours on one RTX 4090 capped at 12 GB VRAM. The 71.21% result includes enhanced search and experience priors; it is not the isolated weight-training effect.

works.title: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement

publication.actor: Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5) and Codex (gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra) research agents; Claude Opus 4.8 fixed rollout model; LoRA SFT of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base via Tinker
publication.summary: Isolates training-data research by holding the model, training infrastructure and evaluation stack fixed.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Research agents form capability hypotheses, construct training data, inspect checkpoint feedback and select a final checkpoint under a bounded budget. Traces preserve the research decisions.
Results and comparison

The paper reports improvement over the first valid attempt in 58.33% of settings (14 of 24). Among searches continuing beyond their observed peak, 78.26% (18 of 23) finish with a lower-scoring final attempt; the rest recover the same peak.
Evaluation context

The post-peak statistic is conditional on continuing search, not all runs. Reporting best-found and selected-final checkpoints separately makes candidate discovery and checkpoint retention distinguishable. Each of the 24 agent-benchmark settings has one representative run.

works.title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
works.short_title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents

publication.actor: GPT-5-mini as both agent backbone and memory-construction model
publication.summary: Tests how memory-based agent improvements depend on random runs, curriculum and environmental specifications.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

Re-evaluates two memory methods (Agent Workflow Memory and ReasoningBank) on WebArena, VisualWebArena and SCUBA across multiple runs and shuffled task streams, then studies more explicit task rubrics and environment feedback during memory construction.
Results and comparison

In the reported ReasoningBank comparison, a +1.5 percentage-point gain under default ordering becomes a 4.5-point loss under shuffled orders. On the WebArena GitLab subset (180 tasks, three runs), the best-to-worst run gap expands from 4.4 points for the baseline to 7.8 with memory.
Evaluation context
These results concern the evaluated agents and task streams. Better specifications partly recover performance; they do not establish that memory is uniformly harmful.

works.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
works.short_title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents

publication.actor: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4 mini as code, debugger and meta agents on Terminal-Bench; Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6 Terra (ARC-AGI-3) and GPT-5.4 (EdgeBench) for games
publication.summary: Compares harness evolution with parallel sampling and sequential refinement under matched budgets, on held-out Terminal-Bench tasks and long-horizon games.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks) experiments compare AHE-based harness evolution and per-task harness scaling with parallel sampling and sequential refinement at a matched budget of K=5, with and without unit-test feedback, and test transfer on a 45/10/34 train/validation/test split. Version 4 adds long-horizon games (25 public ARC-AGI-3 games and five EdgeBench game tasks) that start from engineered harnesses.
Results and comparison

On Terminal-Bench, harness evolution does not outperform the test-time baselines with or without unit tests. On the 34 held-out tasks it changes pass@1 by +1.2 (Claude Opus 4.6), 0.0 (GPT-5.4) and -1.4 (GPT-5.4 mini) points, averaging 0.0 in v4 (v1 reported two models, averaging +0.6). On ARC-AGI-3, full-harness scaling raises RHAE from 43.3 to 77.5 (Opus 4.8) and from 21.1 to 38.2 (GPT-5.6 Terra) over sequential refinement with the VISTA* harness; EdgeBench averages rise from 48.3 to 54.7 and from 45.9 to 49.8.
Evaluation context

Terminal-Bench results average two runs and instantiate harness evolution with AHE without its explore agent. The game gains come from task-specific harness scaling rather than a transferable harness, report the best score within matched action or wall-clock budgets, and use different models from the Terminal-Bench study. The findings motivate reporting search/evaluation overlap and matched-budget baselines rather than ranking all harness-evolution methods by one study.

works.title: Knowledge-Centric Self-Improvement

publication.actor: Claude Agent SDK with Haiku 4.5 and OpenAI Agents SDK with GPT-5.4-mini (medium reasoning); the same models run the forum and distillation phases
publication.summary: Makes a shared, curated knowledge base the object retained across otherwise disposable agents.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Agents contribute evidence-grounded findings to task and cross-task forums, followed by distillation. The evaluation includes budget-matched prompt-optimization baselines and cross-model reuse.
Results and comparison
The paper reports improved solve rates and lower listed costs across abstract reasoning, coding and terminal tasks, with knowledge transfer to held-out tasks and other model families.
Evaluation context

The persistent artifact is knowledge, while agents remain generic. Model roles and evaluation regimes differ across comparisons; improvements should be read per benchmark rather than as one universal gain.

works.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey

publication.actor: Not applicable: conceptual or survey contribution
publication.summary: Organizes persistent agent updates by the component changed and the feedback that drives them.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Treats an agent as a foundation model coupled to prompts, memory, tools and control logic; describes an update operator over model parameters or scaffold components.
Results and comparison
Provides a literature framework connecting applications and evaluation questions. This is a survey contribution rather than a new measured speedup or autonomous research experiment.
Evaluation context
Its component-based view complements this collection’s community/object categories. A memory or harness mechanism can appear in systems, model-development or agent work without duplicating the paper.

works.title: The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement

publication.actor: Not applicable: conceptual or survey contribution
publication.summary: Models when AI-assisted research could produce sustained acceleration rather than improvements within a fixed task.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Directed feedback graphs connect research inputs, narrow AI-R&D ability and broader economically useful capability through loop elasticities.
Results and comparison
A tentative calibration puts a self-sustaining threshold near 15% R&D-productivity gain per capability-index unit, compared with an approximately 9% estimate from available uplift evidence.
Evaluation context

These are model-dependent, back-of-the-envelope estimates with substantial uncertainty, not an experimental measurement of a universal RSI threshold. The paper proposes empirical quantities that would improve calibration.

works.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution
works.short_title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

publication.actor: The Qwen3 policy being trained also extracts, merges and validates experience under dedicated prompts and serves as its own experience-conditioned teacher; no external model is used.
publication.target: Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B base models; AIME24, AIME25, GSM8K, MATH500 and MINA
publication.summary: Builds a validated experience pool, distills it into model weights and follows with reward-driven optimization.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Experience is extracted from successful and failed rollouts, consolidated and validated before privileged self-distillation and GRPO.
Results and comparison

Qwen3-8B average accuracy across five math benchmarks rises from 32.18% to 38.71%. Removing stage II gives 36.14%; removing the shared pool gives 35.48%. The study reports approximately 28% fewer training trajectories at matched performance versus GRPO.
Evaluation context
Accuracy, sampling success and training-trajectory count are distinct metrics. The trajectory reduction is not a measured 28% reduction in total compute.

works.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills

publication.actor: Model roles vary by experiment; exact configurations were not extracted in this review.
publication.summary: Co-evolves a skill library, task proposer and solver using executable task checks.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
The proposer creates tasks conditioned on reusable skills and validators. The solver learns with GRPO; proposer rewards favor valid tasks near its current ability frontier.
Results and comparison

Evaluates five 3B–14B backbones over five iterations on tool calling and logical reasoning, with base-model and unguided-self-play comparisons and mechanism ablations. Final benchmark results use avg@8.
Evaluation context

The same checkpoint initializes proposer and solver. Unguided self-play cannot form a viable reasoning curriculum in this setup and is compared only on tool calling; that missing comparison should remain explicit.

works.title: AI4AI at Test-Time: Strong-to-Weak Capability Transfer via Harnesses

publication.actor: Model roles vary by experiment; exact configurations were not extracted in this review.
publication.target: GPT-5.4-mini in the main reported comparison
publication.summary: Uses stronger builder models to improve weaker target models through executable harnesses without changing weights.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Builders refine harnesses using 5% validation data from four Theory-of-Mind benchmarks. Analysis distinguishes deterministic code, routing and formatting from additional model reasoning.
Results and comparison
Across 57 scaffolded GPT-5.4-mini runs, mean macro accuracy is 0.763, a +0.275 uplift. The best individual run reaches 0.912; that maximum is not the average outcome.
Evaluation context
The experiment evaluates task-specific harness construction. Builder and target are distinct roles, and comparisons to a human-designed harness remain task-dependent.

works.title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks

publication.actor: Model roles vary by experiment; exact configurations were not extracted in this review.
publication.summary: Distributes decision rules across training tasks and recombines them in held-out business workflows.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
An automated construction pipeline separates generation and review, controls the supervision supplied during evolution, and tests transfer of retained skills.
Results and comparison
The paper reports positive evolution gains but a substantial gap to a fully informed oracle ceiling of 91.6%. It releases benchmark construction and evaluation artifacts.
Evaluation context

The oracle receives information unavailable to ordinary agents; its score is an information-rich ceiling rather than a matched baseline. Rule recombination tests a designed transfer relation, not every form of business generalization.

works.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

publication.actor: Model roles vary by experiment; exact configurations were not extracted in this review.
publication.summary: Uses matched persistence-on and persistence-off runs to test whether retained experience helps future episodes.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
The benchmark includes 204 episodes across 26 task-family scenarios and four capability dimensions. Trace-backed mechanism scores accompany behavioral gains.
Results and comparison

The study compares personal-agent frameworks and performs mechanism-level changes to Hermes. Some component combinations help particular dimensions, while the overall Hermes/Hermes+ gain difference is smaller than run-to-run variation.
Evaluation context

This measures foundations of persistent adaptation across episode sequences. Mechanism evidence and performance deltas should be read together; successful retention alone does not establish improved research efficiency.

works.title: S3Gym: Can LLMs Turn Self-Testing and Self-Judging into Self-Improvement?

publication.actor: Model roles vary by experiment; exact configurations were not extracted in this review.
publication.summary: Separates exploration from held-out play to compare raw history, summarized memory and weight training.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Seven text games provide executable verifiers and distinct exploration/evaluation configurations. Experiments inspect self-judgment and how experience changes subsequent behavior.
Results and comparison

History, summaries and training produce task-dependent outcomes. Summaries help when strategic rules compress well; raw history can work better when exact state information matters. Parameter training also produces negative transfer in some settings.
Evaluation context
The games offer controlled feedback, not open-ended research tasks. The study makes the choice of retained representation an experimentally testable variable.

works.title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement

publication.actor: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Preview and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 during evolution
publication.summary: Evolves separate harness modules using contrasting successful and failed trajectories and validation gates.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

Module edits pass local checks before cross-module integration. Evolution uses 120 terminal-related and 120 software-related instances selected from a 2,000-instance curated dataset, over three epochs.
Results and comparison
Evaluation reports accuracy, pass@3, all-three-success consistency and interaction steps, including benchmark-disjoint and cross-model transfer analyses.
Evaluation context
The paper does not provide a dedicated ablation isolating contrastive trajectory analysis. Keep the full mechanism’s results separate from causal claims about that component.

works.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out

publication.actor: Model roles vary by experiment; exact configurations were not extracted in this review.
publication.summary: Connects grounded research ideas to implementation, diagnosis and independent review of experiment artifacts.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
A dependency graph coordinates executable research tasks; persistent state records results and evidence-based decisions to continue, revise or terminate a direction.
Results and comparison

In the RSICD retrieval case study, reported mean Recall improves from 32.84 to 34.69. The audit records five confirmed issue events for this system versus 11–27 for the compared autonomous research systems.
Evaluation context
These are case-study and audit outcomes, not a common-budget estimate of general research acceleration. The paper also studies systems optimization and benchmark-driven machine learning.

works.title: Intology Locus: Scaling Automated Post-Training

publication.actor: Locus with Opus 5 in the reported Tier 1 comparison; other settings use different configurations.
publication.summary: Runs parallel, multi-day post-training experiments and reports both benchmark and production outcomes.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Locus searches model-training choices with dedicated experimentation infrastructure. The blog separates official PostTrainBench settings from a larger-compute PostTrainBench+ study.
Results and comparison
In the reported Tier 1 comparison, Locus with Opus 5 scores 44.7 versus 41.8 for Claude Code with Fable 5. A separate Bubble deployment reports lower error, latency and cost.
Evaluation context

The headline Tier 1 comparison changes both model and harness. Larger-budget results and the Bubble deployment have different conditions; they are not interchangeable estimates of a single effect. This entry records an industry report.

works.title: XYZ-Aquila: AI4AI at Scale

publication.actor: Development-agent identifiers are not specified in the inspected blog; target backbones are Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.
publication.summary: Uses gated interventions across data, training, runtime and context management to develop open-weight search agents.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

Humans define objectives and acceptance criteria; agents diagnose failures and propose changes. Accepted and rejected attempts become auditable experience; external benchmarks are withheld from routine optimization.
Results and comparison
The blog reports seven search benchmarks for mini/pro systems. XYZ-Aquila-mini achieves 78.8% BrowseComp accuracy and 89.5 DeepSearchQA F1 in the reported setup.
Evaluation context

The results evaluate the final configurations, not isolated contributions of each intervention. Some baselines use different stacks or dates. The screened process-reward RL extension is excluded from the released systems.

works.title: IntentLab: Turn Your Intent into Production Systems

publication.actor: IntentLab autonomous fleet; underlying model identifiers are not specified in the inspected blog.
publication.summary: An autonomous engineering fleet combines system design, implementation and verification for specialized software.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
The inference case re-engineers TensorRT-LLM for GLM 5.2 on Grace Blackwell nodes, combining kernel, runtime and communication changes with DSpark speculative decoding.
Results and comparison
The blog reports 102 output tokens/s for stock TensorRT-LLM, 161 after runtime optimization, and 647 with DSpark, approximately 6.3× the starting throughput.
Evaluation context

The total combines several interventions, including speculative decoding. The inspected page does not specify a complete batch, sequence-length, precision and search-cost protocol; treat it as an industry case report, not a directly comparable serving benchmark.

works.title: OpenRSI Index: An Open Benchmark for Model-Development Research

publication.actor: Task-dependent research agents, including Codex and Claude Code in the preview examples.
publication.summary: Packages open model-development projects as bounded research environments with separate verifiers and released trajectories.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

RSI-Harness keeps a persistent Work environment and evaluates snapshots in fresh Judge containers. Tasks specify editable boundaries, budgets and reference recipes; the best valid submission is retained.
Results and comparison

The preview includes optimizer scaling, visual generation, 122B post-training and smaller systems/agent tasks. Its Qwen task reports a five-benchmark geometric mean of 71.51 for agent-generated data versus 71.37 for the baseline, with mixed per-domain outcomes.
Evaluation context

This is an evolving preview, not a finalized leaderboard. The website and repository contain changing task descriptions and resource requirements; pin the task revision before comparing results. The Qwen headline gain is 0.14 points over the baseline, not the +0.42 points measured against the starting model.

works.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness

publication.actor: Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro and GLM 5.3 in the nanoGPT harness comparison.
publication.summary: Combines a persistent Python control environment with revisable prompts, memories, skills and subagent specifications.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure

A persistent Python environment supports tool orchestration and revisable prompts, memory, skills and subagent specifications. nanoGPT evaluates research on a 124M-parameter target, with each record checked as an eight-seed mean.
Results and comparison

Across 18 nanoGPT runs, the paper finds little harness effect on final records relative to experimental noise. DeepSeek V4 Pro creates roughly six times more out-of-training-script experiments per training run in Prime Agent than in Claude Code.
Evaluation context

Experiment counts are manually classified, with denominators audited where possible and otherwise estimated from launch commands. The result distinguishes changed research behavior from demonstrated final-score gains. Other benchmark comparisons use different models and budgets.

works.title: ShinkaEvolve: Open Program Evolution

publication.actor: Configurable LLM mutation ensemble with external fitness evaluation.
publication.summary: Maintains program populations and evaluated archives for LLM-guided scientific-code search.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
LLMs propose program mutations; an external evaluator supplies fitness. The repository supports parallel candidate evaluation, archives and evolving islands across local and cluster workflows.
Results and comparison
The launch blog reports a 26-circle packing solution found with 150 samples and an agent-scaffold experiment over 75 generations, including transfer tests.
Evaluation context
These are distinct tasks and budgets. Sample efficiency is not automatically dollar or wall-clock efficiency; current repository features are tracked separately from the 2025 launch results.

works.title: GEPA: Reflective Optimization of Prompts, Code and Agent Systems

publication.actor: Configurable reflection model and target system; optimizer and target can differ.
publication.summary: Combines trace-based reflection with Pareto-aware evolution over textual system parameters.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
The optimizer reads execution feedback to propose targeted edits, evaluates variants and preserves useful tradeoffs. The interface spans prompts, code, configurations and agent architectures.
Results and comparison
The maintained implementation exposes optimization and evaluation interfaces, examples and application reports. Reported benefits depend on the task, evaluator and optimization budget.
Evaluation context
This entry covers the ongoing framework. The Databricks enterprise case has a separate record because its model comparison, serving costs and held-out workload require their own experimental context.

works.title: Databricks Agent Bricks: Automated Prompt Optimization on IE Bench

publication.actor: gpt-oss-120b and Claude Sonnet 4 optimizers; targets include gpt-oss-120b and Claude models.
publication.summary: Evaluates automated prompts on held-out enterprise information-extraction tasks and separates search from serving cost.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Compares GEPA, SIMBA and MIPROv2, including gpt-oss-120b as both optimizer and target and Claude Sonnet 4 as a stronger optimizer. A separate subset compares prompt optimization with SFT.
Results and comparison
The best GEPA-optimized gpt-oss-120b configuration gains 4.3 points over its baseline and 2.2 points over baseline Claude Opus 4.1. The reported roughly 90× cost advantage concerns serving.
Evaluation context

The cost estimate uses then-published prices and measured token distributions; it is not a current price quote or a 90× reduction in total research expenditure. The study separately discusses optimization overhead and amortization.

works.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation

publication.actor: Qwen and OLMo targets from 1.7B to 8B; no external teacher
publication.summary: Alternates verifiable-reward learning with distillation from an extrapolation of the model’s own training trajectory.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Constructs token-level targets from the displacement between current and anchor checkpoints, in weight or logit space. The teacher is refreshed each iteration; rollout samples are reused.
Results and comparison
Across three seeds, Qwen3-8B Math Avg is 62.4±0.2 versus GRPO’s 60.1±0.2. A separate gradient-budget-matched comparison reports 62.7 versus 60.5 for GRPO with two update passes.
Evaluation context

The additional distillation phase costs approximately 1.3–1.6× GRPO wall time per iteration. Removing reward grounding collapses MATH-500 accuracy to 2.4%; directly adopting extrapolated weights gives little average gain. Reward reliability remains a dependency.

works.title: Experience Funnel: A State–Policy Alternating Loop for Self-Evolving Agents

publication.actor: Qwen3.5-4B deployment policy; fixed Qwen3.5-27B distillation teacher; Ascend 910B3
publication.summary: Alternates editable skills and harness state with distillation into a deployment policy.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Validation gates state revisions before policy consolidation. Five state rounds produce two accepted updates; training, validation and final test splits have separate roles.
Results and comparison
On SearchQA, state-free accuracy rises from 58.1% to 61.3%; the matched evolved state and policy reaches 62.4%. Applying that evolved state to the initial policy gives 60.2%.
Evaluation context

Table 2 reports a separate 63.6% full-loop ablation, which should not replace Table 1’s 62.4% main result. ALFWorld and WebShop use different distillation budgets. Most intermediate configurations are single runs; repeated-run uncertainty is supplied for the final comparison.

works.title: EvoAgentBench: Benchmarking Agent Self-Evolution via Ability Transfer

publication.actor: OpenClaw and Nanobot; Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-397B and Gemma-4-31B evaluation backbones
publication.summary: Constructs train/test relations around reusable abilities to measure transfer from retained agent experience.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
Compares case retrieval, reasoning memory and GEPA prompts across four domains, two scaffolds and three backbones. Tests use three independent runs per instance.
Results and comparison
Every automatic method has a negative-transfer cell. GEPA’s domain-and-scaffold average improves by 1.2, 3.5 and 5.7 points across the three backbones, while four individual cells regress.
Evaluation context

The Anchor Skill diagnostic uses curator-side routing labels unavailable to automatic methods. Its uniformly positive results are a diagnostic reference. Test tasks are selected for support and remaining headroom, so absolute gains do not estimate a random task population.

works.title: LIMBO: Lifelong Inference-Time Memory and Budget Optimization for LLM Agents

publication.actor: Qwen2.5-7B, Llama3.1-8B and GPT-4o mini
publication.summary: Learns when retained experience is useful and how much inference budget to spend on each task.
details: Method and supplied infrastructure
A contextual bandit chooses among no memory, full replay, compressed replay and retrieval, paired with budget tiers. Evaluation uses two 500-task LifelongAgentBench streams and three matched seeds.
Results and comparison

Across six model/environment settings, reported token-cost reductions are 26–83% against the strongest memory baseline, with accuracy differences ranging from −3.8 to +0.6 points. On Llama DB, accuracy reaches 66.2% versus 20.8% without replay.
Evaluation context

Local-model dollar costs use standardized token-price proxies, not measured serving expense. The largest savings occur where memory adds little accuracy. The method updates the allocation controller without changing the underlying language-model weights.
