Rethinking Harness Evaluation's v4 finds no average held-out gain on 34 Terminal-Bench tasks (+1.2, 0.0 and −1.4 points across three models), while task-specific harness scaling raises ARC-AGI-3 scores from 43.3 to 77.5.
insights.interpretation: Our reading: strong evolution-set performance and transferable improvements are different outcomes. These papers make selection rules and evaluation protocols central research objects.
insights.experiment: Hold the backbone, starting harness and candidate budget fixed. Compare unrestricted edits, sparse edits and stability-aware acceptance on unseen task families; repeat full searches across seeds and report uncertainty.

insights.title: Persistent experience needs a task-stream test
insights.evidence: The fragility study changes a +1.5-point memory gain into a 4.5-point loss by shuffling task order. Knowledge-Centric Self-Improvement studies portable knowledge rather than one persistent agent.
insights.interpretation: Our reading: a useful memory should retain applicable constraints as well as successful actions. A single curriculum can hide sensitivity to what the agent encounters next.
insights.experiment: Compare no memory, raw trajectories, distilled knowledge and condition-aware retrieval on identical shuffled streams. Track cost, cross-model reuse, forgetting and changes in performance after each domain switch.

insights.title: Separate the researcher, the harness and the trained model
insights.evidence: Frontis-MA1 evaluates model and harness swaps. Co-Harness updates both components, while AI4AI at Test-Time keeps target weights fixed and changes an external harness.
insights.interpretation: Our reading: “the model improved” can describe several distinct changes. Recording actor and target roles makes cross-community comparisons more informative.
insights.experiment: Run a two-by-two study with original/improved weights and original/improved harnesses. Keep data and evaluation fixed; add an unseen backbone to distinguish weight-specific adaptation from reusable procedures.

insights.title: Research efficiency and deployment efficiency have different costs
insights.evidence: AIDE² constrains inner evaluation expenditure. KernelGenBench accounts for tokens per successful operator. Databricks separates prompt-search overhead from serving-cost estimates.
insights.interpretation: Our reading: faster or cheaper artifacts can still require substantial research expenditure. A fixed inner budget does not erase the outer search cost.
insights.experiment: Report total proposal, execution, evaluator and review costs. Plot held-out artifact quality against cumulative research spend, then estimate the deployment volume needed to recover that investment.

insights.title: Treat scale transfer as part of the experimental contract
insights.evidence: OpenRSI’s optimizer task keeps one rule across a model-size ladder. KernelGenBench measures accelerator portability; compiler-grounded Triton reports results on a successful-conversion subset.
insights.interpretation: Our reading: model scale, hardware and successful-conversion coverage are separate axes. An average over a selected subset can answer a narrower question than a full-suite result.
insights.experiment: Choose the development hardware and small-model screens in advance. Freeze the selected method before evaluating larger models or unseen accelerators; count unsupported and failed cases alongside successful results.

insights.title: Finding a good candidate and retaining it are separate skills
insights.evidence: RSIBench-Data reports post-peak regressions in 78.26% of searches that continue past their best observed attempt. OpenRSI’s harness retains the best valid submission.
insights.interpretation: Our reading: search progress depends on checkpoint selection and reliable re-evaluation, not just generating additional ideas.
insights.experiment: Compare last-candidate, best-observed and independently rechecked selection with the same search traces. Use fresh evaluation seeds and report both best-discovered and finally delivered performance.

insights.title: A shared mechanism can connect different research communities
insights.evidence: The companion lists emphasize persistent state, harness evolution, verifiers and loop closure. Here, systems, kernels, model development and agent research remain distinct primary categories.
insights.interpretation: Our synthesis: use the community/object category as the paper’s home, then compare change mechanism and feedback path across homes. This preserves differences without assigning a single RSI quality score.
insights.experiment: Test whether an improved research procedure helps solve new problems under the same resource budget. Keep artifact improvement, transfer of the procedure and improvement of the improver as separate measured outcomes.

insights.title: Separate retained guidance from competence absorbed into weights
insights.evidence: Experience Funnel tests evolved state with both initial and updated policies. RISE includes a gradient-budget-matched baseline and ablations of reward grounding and distillation.
insights.interpretation: “Self-improvement” can refer to different storage locations and feedback signals. A stronger combined agent does not by itself identify which component learned.
insights.experiment: Cross initial/evolved state with initial/updated weights on the same held-out tasks. Include a state-free evaluation and match gradient updates, rollout tokens and wall time separately.

insights.title: Useful experience depends on routing and its inference cost
insights.evidence: EvoAgentBench finds negative-transfer cells despite positive method averages; its curator-routed diagnostic is not a deployable baseline. LIMBO measures memory selection against both accuracy and token cost.
insights.interpretation: A memory can contain useful information but still be selected at the wrong time or cost more than its benefit. Retention, retrieval and execution should be measured separately.
insights.experiment: Hold memory contents fixed and compare no retrieval, random retrieval, learned routing and curator routing. Report per-domain accuracy, added tokens and failure types across multiple task orders.

reading_context.window: New work through 2026-10-07, extending the original 2026-06-25 to 2026-09-25 window. Foundational work from 2023 to 2025 was backfilled in the 2026-10-07 update.
reading_context.method: Date-bounded arXiv web searches across the seven research directions, cross-checked against four community lists and original papers. The 2026-10-07 update added alphaXiv topic discovery across thirteen themes; each candidate was read in full text against a written scope rule and the loop-profile vocabulary, and existing entries were relabeled and checked against their primary sources. Experiments were not independently reproduced.
reading_context.coverage: A targeted literature scan, not an exhaustive arXiv census. The original pass could not use the arXiv API (HTTP 406) and relied on indexed arXiv pages and bibliography links. Out-of-scope candidates, such as domain applications of self-improvement, were excluded. Numbers follow the cited version of each paper; when versions disagree, the entry says which it uses. Older ongoing projects and industry reports are dated separately.
